in_arabic.name: زوار
in_arabic.long_meaning: زوار هو اسم عربي مشتق من الفعل زار، يعني الزيارة أو القدوم على شخص أو مكان، وهو مصطلح له أهمية كبيرة في الثقافة الإسلامية حيث يُشير إلى الزيارة للمساجد والمقدسات أو زيارة الأحباء والأقارب

in_urdu.name: زوار
in_urdu.long_meaning: زوار عربی gốc کا نام ہے جو زار سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے کہ کسی شخص یا جگہ کی زیارت کرنا، اور یہ اصطلاح اسلامی ثقافت میں بہت اہم ہے جہاں یہ مساجد اور مقدس مقامات کی زیارت یا رشتہ داروں اور احباء کی زیارت کرنے کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے

data.cultural_impact: The name Zawwar holds great cultural significance in the Islamic tradition, as it is often associated with the bravery, determination, and self-sacrifice of those who fight in the name of Allah. This name reflects the important role of jihad (struggle in the way of Allah) in the Islamic faith and the commitment to defend Islam and promote justice, peace, and mercy.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Zawwar underscores the idea of struggling to overcome one's own inner adversities and striving for personal growth and self-improvement in the service of Allah. This name reminds us of the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) who encouraged Muslims to strive against their own baser selves and to focus on their faith, piety, and obedience to Allah. In essence, Zawwar represents not only a warrior in the physical sense but also a spiritual warrior continuously fighting against their own negative traits and vices, as they seek to please and draw closer to Allah.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, vol. 15, p. 60-61 The name Zawwar carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Zawwar ibn Hassan, a Turkish slave, became the governor of Damascus for the Ayyubid Sultan Al-Nasir Yusuf. He was a shrewd and capable administrator, and during his rule, Damascus experienced a period of peace and prosperity.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqrizi's The History of Iraq (Kitab al-Mawasit al-'Iraqiyyah), vol. 3, p. 519 The name Zawwar carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Zawwar ibn Ahmad al-Harrasi was a powerful and wealthy Sufi sheikh who lived during the Mamluk Sultanate. He was known for his ascetic practices and his ability to perform miracles. Many pilgrims came to visit him, and he was highly respected by both the Mamluk rulers and the common people.
